summary.intent: Fix failing CI for both web and desktop E2E tests in the cipher-box repo, specifically diagnosing why the desktop FUSE file upload/publish pipeline never triggers after a file write.
summary.outcome: Web E2E was essentially fixed (175/176 passing, 1 flaky Sapphire login). Desktop FUSE drain fix was identified and implemented: added `drain_upload_completions()` to the macOS/Linux readdir handler and added `ls` calls to test scripts to force a FUSE readdir after writes, then committed and pushed to CI.

repo: Windows dir_ops.rs had drain_upload_completions() in its readdir handler but macOS/Linux dir_ops.rs did not — a platform-specific divergence causing silent upload pipeline failures on non-Windows CI.
The FUSE write -> upload -> publish chain requires an explicit drain trigger; without a subsequent FUSE operation (like readdir/ls), upload completions are never processed after release().
Desktop FUSE failures pre-date PR #448 and were already present since PR #446 — not a regression introduced in the current work.
Web E2E has a flaky Sapphire login test that fails non-deterministically across runs.

code.finding: Windows dir_ops.rs has drain_upload_completions() in readdir; macOS/Linux equivalent was missing this call, breaking the upload pipeline in CI.
Added ls of mount point after file write to force a FUSE readdir operation, which triggers drain_upload_completions() and unblocks the upload pipeline.
Same ls/dir fix applied to PowerShell script for Windows parity.

workflow: Polling CI logs for Rust app output (zero publish-related log lines) was the key diagnostic that distinguished a timeout issue from a pipeline-never-firing issue.
Doubling polling timeouts (to 120s) was a red herring — the root cause was the drain never being called, not insufficient wait time.

friction: CI failures were misleading — doubling timeouts to 120s was attempted first before discovering the pipeline never fired at all.
Platform divergence between Windows and macOS/Linux FUSE implementations was not obvious and required grep-based discovery.
Flaky Sapphire login in web E2E adds noise to CI results, making it harder to confirm a clean green run.
open_items: CI result for the FUSE drain fix commit was not yet confirmed — need to verify the desktop tests pass after the push.
The flaky web E2E Sapphire login test (1/176 failing non-deterministically) was not addressed and should be investigated or marked as known-flaky.
Root cause of why macOS/Linux dir_ops.rs diverged from Windows (missing drain_upload_completions) should be reviewed to prevent similar platform-specific gaps.
